name: The Waking and the Year of Ashfall
summary: The current age's turning: after four centuries of comfortable forgetting, Glimmerborn began being born again — first one, in a Dusk Reach village, then three more within the year. The Censer's hunts doubled; the Quiet's advance quickened; the sealed places started to ring. In 812 AA, ash from an un-named mountain dusted the Crownlands, a page of the Song Unbinding surfaced in the Hollow Mile, and the Censer split against itself over whether the returning song is a plague or a promise. Nobody calls it a crisis yet. Everybody prepares like one.

course_of_events.what: A Dusk Reach village girl hums a note no one taught her and the well-water rises an inch. The Censer takes her. Before year's end, three more Glimmerborn surface across three realms. The Grey Peace ends quietly, like a held breath released.

Births rise yearly. The Quiet advances by hands' widths instead of fingers. Hallord seals a ringing shaft; the Storm-Bound hear the sea sing; Karvess's towers change their note. Each realm explains it locally. The patterns match.

Ash from an un-named mountain dusts the Crownlands on Goldharvest. The Quiet advances two hand-widths. A page of the Song Unbinding sells in the Hollow Mile for a king's ransom — possibly genuine. Three buyers are dead. The seller has vanished.

The First-Heard sect's leaks reach the Rememberers; the Nine Ashes schedule a purge vote. For the first time since its founding oath, the Censer may draw blades on itself. The Reeve's court waits, coin in hand, for whichever side wins.

key_places.name: The Waking Village
key_places.description: The Dusk Reach village where the first new Glimmerborn was found. The well still rises an inch when certain notes are sung nearby; the Censer keeps a permanent warden there now.

key_places.name: The Un-Named Mountain
key_places.description: Source of the 812 ashfall — it appears on no map. Ash-line analysis points somewhere east of the Stone Crown, into country no survey returns from.

key_places.name: The Singing Places
key_places.description: Hallord's sealed shaft, the Veiled Sea past the horizon, Karvess's towers, the Deep-Forging's anvil-note: all sounding the same tone now, at intervals that are shortening.

key_places.name: The Mile's Dead Buyers' Row
key_places.description: Three purchasers of the Song Unbinding page died within a season — each differently, each with the page one room away. The fourth copy is the one for sale.

consequences: The Grey Peace is over: fear is policy again in every chancery.
The Censer faces its first internal schism in 812 years.
Every faction is positioning for something — revival, purge, profit, or proof.
The Last Weaver prophecy has stopped being mythology: someone appears to be searching for that voice.
remembrance: Too current for remembrance — this is the story players walk into. The Road-Singers' spreading ballad about the ashfall contains details no singer should know.
adventure_hooks: Players hold the deciding testimony at the tide-moot or the purge vote — factions begin courting them before they understand the stakes.
Finding the un-named mountain answers whether the ash is death or birth; both expeditions already forming want the same guides.
The vanished seller of the Song Unbinding page contacts players: they will give the page free — to whoever swears to read it aloud at the Stone Crown's seal.
